column1: # WHICH ASSEMBLIES THE DOUBLE LEDGER LOOKS AT, and what looks at them.
# docs/TEST-ARCHITECTURE-PLAN.md 3.2, rung-1 assertion 4. This file is the answer to the escape
# the first design could not close: "put the fake in a project the ledger does not look at".
# Adding a [Double] to a project with no row here reddens `dev lint` until either the project is
# given rung-2 coverage or the double moves. The scan that reads this is TEXT, not reflection, so
# it cannot miss an assembly the way a runtime enumeration silently did.
# rung2 is the test project whose DoubleLedgerTests loads that assembly, or the literal word
# `corpus` for a double anchored by recorded bytes rather than by types.
# ASCII, CRLF, no BOM, tab-separated. tests\ledger\README.md says why.

D-T27: a program, not a type. Anchoring a 545-line exe by reflecting over one of its classes asserts nothing about the wire shapes it emits, which is the only thing anyone cares about. Its anchor is MANIFEST.json + dev wire-sample + lint row I9, file-based end to end, so [Double] is NOT linked in here (D-B7).
